title: Iodine clock: 1/t against volume of H2O2
summary: Four test tubes with different volumes of 0.2 M H2O2(aq) (topped up with distilled water) turn dark blue at different times; 1/t is proportional to rate. A graph of 1/t against volume of H2O2 added is a straight line through the origin, so the reaction is first order with respect to H2O2(aq).

blocks.text: Table: Test tube | Volume of 0.2 M H2O2(aq) added (cm3) [handwritten: ∝ [H2O2(aq)]] | Volume of distilled water added (cm3) | Time for the appearance of the dark blue colour when H2O2(aq) added are mixed (s) | 1/t [handwritten: ∝ rate]. Rows 1-4 as in data.
Red: 1/t ∝ rate (star); ∝ [H2O2(aq)] under the volume column header; small axes 'rate' vs '[A]' at right
Graph: y = 1/time (s^-1), 0.0100 to 0.0600; x = Volume of H2O2(aq) added (cm3), 0 to 5. Straight line from the origin through 4 points at x = 1, 2, 3, 4.
From the graph, a straight line passing through the origin is obtained. The reaction is first order with respect to H2O2(aq).

columns: Time for appearance of dark blue colour (s)

graph.line: straight line passing through the origin (0,0) and the 4 points, ending at (4, 0.0500)

key_concepts: Time for dark blue to appear (clock time) is inversely related to rate; 1/t ∝ rate
Volume of 0.2 M H2O2 added ∝ [H2O2(aq)] (distilled water keeps total volume constant)
Straight line through the origin for 1/t against volume means first order with respect to H2O2
Doubling the volume of H2O2 roughly halves the time

animation.concept: A race of four test tubes: more H2O2 means a shorter time to the sudden dark blue, so a larger 1/t (rate), and the finishing times give a straight-line graph.
animation.why: The data come from four parallel experiments, so showing four test tubes turning blue at different times makes the link between concentration, time and 1/t tangible, and it differs from the single-beaker mechanism animation on page 7.

steps.visual: Four glass test tubes (cylinders with rounded bottoms) stand in a rack (a box with four holes), numbered 1-4. Each contains clear liquid at the same height, labelled below: H2O2 1.0 / 2.0 / 3.0 / 4.0 cm3 and water 24.0 / 23.0 / 22.0 / 21.0 cm3. Small stacked blocks beside each tube show the H2O2 portion (blue-white) vs water portion (clear) of total 25.0 cm3.
steps.caption: Same total volume, more 0.2 M H2O2 from tube 1 to 4

steps.visual: A stopwatch sprite appears and all four tubes receive H2O2 simultaneously (a drop animation); timer starts at 0 s. Time scale: 1 s of real animation = 4 s of experiment time so that 78 s fits in about 20 s of animation.
steps.caption: Start: all four mixed at t = 0

steps.visual: Tube 4 turns sudden dark blue when the timer reads 20 s; a label '20 s' and '1/t = 0.0500' pops above it. Next tube 3 turns dark blue at 27 s ('1/t = 0.0370').
steps.caption: Tube 4: 20 s. Tube 3: 27 s

steps.visual: Tube 2 turns dark blue at 40 s ('1/t = 0.0250'), then tube 1 at 78 s ('1/t = 0.0128'). Each colour change is abrupt, not gradual. Finish order flags 1st-4th appear over tubes 4, 3, 2, 1.
steps.caption: Tube 2: 40 s. Tube 1: 78 s

steps.visual: A floating 2D panel shows the table with the finishing times; then axes (x 0-5 cm3, y 0-0.0600 s^-1). Four coloured dots fly from each tube to (1, 0.0128), (2, 0.0250), (3, 0.0370), (4, 0.0500).
steps.caption: Plot 1/t against volume of H2O2

steps.visual: A straight line is drawn from the origin (0,0) through the four points, extending to (4, 0.0500). Origin marker pulses.
steps.caption: Straight line through the origin

steps.visual: Text appears over the graph: 'rate ∝ [H2O2]  ->  first order with respect to H2O2(aq)'. Hold, then fade to loop.
steps.caption: First order with respect to H2O2(aq)

elements: test tube rack (box) and 4 test tubes (cylinder + half sphere bottoms) with liquid meshes whose colour switches clear -> dark blue
floating mini-graph: axes x 0-5, y 0-0.0600, 4 point spheres, line from origin
correctness_notes: Total volume is 25.0 cm3 in each tube (volumes of H2O2 + distilled water; the page does not show the other reagents explicitly)
Dark blue appears suddenly, at the moment the fixed amount of S2O3^2- is used up
Straight line through the origin means first order with respect to H2O2(aq); do not claim exactly 2x or 4x times since 78/40 is only approx 2
More H2O2 gives a shorter time and a bigger 1/t
